programs.name: Eviction Prevention Program (EPP)
programs.summary: Pays rent arrears directly to your landlord. Priority goes to households with a court summons, then a Notice to Quit, then anyone paying over 30% of income toward rent.
programs.know: Income at or below 60% of area median income (whole household counts); rent at or below 125% of fair market rent. Apply online or by phone through Project Home of Portland, the statewide administrator. Both you and your landlord must take part in the application.

programs.tag: Behind on rent, not evicted yet
programs.name: Housing Stability Support Program (HSSP)
programs.summary: Pays up to $3,000 a year for a security deposit or back rent, including up to 10 months of rental help at $300 a month, paid to your landlord.
programs.know: Household income must be under 30% of area median income. MaineHousing delegates this program locally; in Cumberland County it is run by ProsperityME.

programs.name: 211 Maine
programs.summary: Free, 24/7 referral line for shelter, warming centers and rent help.
programs.know: Dial 211 (press 6 for homeless services), or text your ZIP code to 898-211.

programs.tag: Must be in a shelter now
programs.name: STEP Rapid Re-Housing
programs.summary: Short-term rental help that tapers down, for people currently staying in a participating emergency shelter.
programs.know: Offered through shelters in 10 counties, including Cumberland. You need a referral from the shelter itself — start with 211 or your shelter.

programs.name: Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher
programs.summary: An ongoing rent subsidy paid to your landlord. Income at or below 50% of area median income (75% of new vouchers go to households at or below 30%).
programs.know: Apply online through the Maine Centralized Waiting List — one application covers MaineHousing and all 20 local housing authorities.

programs.tag: For people who already have a voucher
programs.name: ReStart (Family Self-Sufficiency)
programs.summary: For people who already have a Section 8 voucher: a 5-year plan with career coaching that puts matching funds into savings as your income rises.
programs.know: Ask for the Family Self-Sufficiency Coordinator when you call.

programs.name: Section 811 Project Rental Assistance (PRA)
programs.summary: About 60 units statewide, tied to specific buildings (not portable). For extremely low-income adults 18–61 with a disability, enrolled in a qualifying MaineCare waiver.
programs.know: MaineHousing keeps a non-public list of participating properties and matches you by preferred area once you apply — there's no public way to check whether a unit is open in Westbrook specifically.

programs.name: Section 811 Vouchers
programs.summary: A separate, portable rent subsidy (not tied to one building), issued by MaineHousing.
programs.know: Apply with the 811 Preliminary Application through OADS.

programs.name: Housing Support Funds
programs.summary: A once-a-year lump sum for rent, a deposit, or utilities — usable whether you rent, own, or live in a group home.
programs.know: First-come, first-served; you must reapply every year. Not available if you already have a housing subsidy or live in Shared Living.

programs.name: Where to start for all three
programs.summary: Maine DHHS Office of Aging and Disability Services (OADS) screens applicants for all three disability-housing programs above.
